title: Build route.sequence as ordered {layer}.{action} steps

facts.note: Fires when an acceptance artifact is authored or edited.
Planner writes or changes an acceptance.
Needs a structural diff observer on the acceptance's route.sequence field; until it exists, file_kind+operation over-approximate activation.

fires: Planner authors a new acceptance that includes a route.sequence.
Planner edits the steps or order of an existing acceptance's route.sequence.
doesNotFire: Editing only the acceptance's prose or Given/When/Then text without touching route.sequence.
Coder changes production code with no acceptance artifact change.

when: The planner writes or changes route.sequence.
then: Write route.sequence as ordered {layer}.{action} transitions from the route_step vocabulary, flowing presentation -> application -> domain -> integration as needed (include only the layers the scenario uses; a route triggered from an external integration may start at integration, as in the event flow).
prefer: Event (starts at integration): integration.call_external -> application.aggregate -> domain.mutate -> integration.persist.
avoid: Free-form step names or layers outside presentation/application/domain/integration.

Listing steps unordered or in an order that does not reflect the actual sequence of transitions; do not reject or reorder an integration-initiated route like the event flow just because it begins at integration.
Padding the route with layers the scenario does not need.
why: A fixed {layer}.{action} vocabulary makes the layer flow behind each acceptance explicit and mechanically checkable.
evidence: Every route.sequence entry matches {layer}.{action} and is in the allowed route_step vocabulary.

Steps are ordered as the scenario's transitions occur, consistent with the canonical shapes: command and query flows run presentation -> application -> (domain) -> integration; the event flow starts at integration.call_external and then proceeds application -> domain -> integration.
verifier_detail: route_step term: one {layer}.{action} transition in a route sequence.

Allowed values — presentation: presentation.command, presentation.query, presentation.display; application: application.use_case, application.query, application.aggregate; domain: domain.create, domain.validate, domain.mutate, domain.policy; integration: integration.read, integration.persist, integration.call_external.

Canonical examples: presentation_flow [presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.validate, integration.persist]; query_flow [presentation.query, application.query, integration.read]; event_flow [integration.call_external, application.aggregate, domain.mutate, integration.persist].

Order is not a strict monotonic layer check: layers may be skipped (query_flow omits domain) and an integration step may both open and close a route (event_flow). All three canonical examples must pass any order check.
audit: Original statement: route.sequence is built as ordered {layer}.{action} transitions flowing presentation -> application -> domain -> integration as needed.
